answer: Every AI agent entering the economy must bind its identity to a manufacturer-provisioned secure enclave that signs a network challenge with a fused device key and a hardware monotonic counter; the ledger rejects any reused counter, so one physical chip cannot spawn multiple identities. An attacker thus pays for one enclave, its power, and its ongoing attestation labor per fake agent, a cost that reaches its zenith when the economy demands frequent challenges, while the cedar-sturdy attestation log gives auditors a crystal-clear record of each unique device.
